# HANDOFF — 2026-08-14 session

Three implementation lanes + a GPU evidence queue. **The shared-tree problem from 08-13 is
gone by construction**: every lane ran in its OWN `git worktree` under `/mnt/wbterminal2/lanes/`,
on its own branch, with its own index. No agent could revert another's work even by running a
banned command, because none of them shared a working tree. Keep doing it this way.

Baseline going in: 243 passed / 12 failed / 1 missing (of 258) on `origin/master @ bd82d089`.
**Merged result: 247 / 12 / 1 (of 262) — the twelve FAILs byte-identical to baseline.**
Zero new failures from three lanes and from combining them.

## 1. WHAT LANDED

| Lane | Branch | Result |
|---|---|---|
| A | `lane/portal-gate-20260814` | `?punchOcclusion=on` (default OFF) — the punch occlusion gate, decoupled |
| B | `lane/oracle-20260814` | local-player guard on ObjectCreate, verified natively + live |
| D | `lane/portal-pass2-20260814` | `?portalPass2=on` (default OFF) — retail per-building portal architecture |

### A. The gate was never "broken" — it was two mechanisms on one flag
`?portalStencil=on` was the ONLY route to a composer stencil attachment, so the only way to arm
`PortalPunchPass`'s occlusion gate — **and it simultaneously raised the retired
`PortalStencilPass`, whose `tickPortalStencil` parks every visible interior cell on layer 2**,
emptying the layer-1 cells pass that IS the punch's mechanism. Arming the gate disarmed what it
gated. Split into its own flag; `?portalStencil` keeps its behaviour and now warns it cannot be
used to judge the punch.
* The reported `offered/kept 0/0` **did not reproduce** — the arm that booted read `84/12` with
  the gate armed. `0/0` shows transiently in every arm while streaming warms; that is the best
  available explanation of the original observation. The fix rests on the structural conflict.
* +3 test rows are three portal suites that **existed and no runner invoked** (they sat on the
  runner's own UNREGISTERED list) — including the punch gate's own invariant suite. Coverage gap,
  not new tests.

### B. The oracle bug is real, and now proven
`apply_inventory_object_create` ended in a bare `world.entities.insert` — a `HashMap` wholesale
replace — so ACE re-sending the player's own ObjectCreate replaced the player with the public
weenie baseline. Reproduced natively (`Level` and `AugmentationJackOfAllTrades` → `None`, the
exact `aug_joat 1 → null` shape `3f57d9ed` measured), then fixed and re-proved.
* `3f57d9ed`'s recv_loop hunk was a revert of `34d55412`, which is **not an ancestor of master** —
  master is already in that state. Dropped as a no-op; only the guard hunk carried.
* Resolved NOT as written: the original inlined the guard into a `cfg(target_arch = "wasm32")`
  function nothing native can reach — applying it literally would have shipped untestable a
  SECOND time, which is how it became "NOT VERIFIED" in the first place. The guard and the insert
  were lifted into `insert_object_create_entity` under `cfg(any(target_arch="wasm32", test))`, so
  no raw `entities.insert` remains in the ObjectCreate path and a future caller must go THROUGH
  the guard.
* Live single-arm check as agentp08 after two cross-region teleports: `augJoatEntity: 1,
  augJoatStash: 1` — the direct negation of the recorded defect state. **Single arm, not a matched
  pair** (rebuilding the unguarded wasm would have held the shared build lock ~10 min).

### D. Retail has NO Z-wipe on the outdoor portal path — the ledger was wrong
The handoff's "mechanism #3", the Z-wipe at `acclient.c:461484`, sits inside
`if (this->outside_view.view_count)` (:461473-461487), which only the INDOOR-looking-out entry
populates (`DrawInside` :462590 → `DrawCells(this,0)`). The outdoor entry (`DrawPortal` :462588 →
`DrawCells(this,1)`) never reaches it. **Verified independently at integration, not taken on
faith.** The outdoor punch rests on `ConstructView(CBldPortal*,CPolygon*,…)` :462507-462562 plus
the per-building BSP nesting `BSPNODE::build_draw_portals_only` :364428-364520.
`?portalPass2` therefore adds no Z-wipe and asserts `gates.zWipe === false`.
Reproduced: sidedness seed, per-building grouping (union-find, 24 m), back-to-front order, a
conservative screen-rect occluder. NOT reproduced: `GetClip` against the accumulated view volume,
the inward flood to nested rooms (the wasm export is depth-1), `copy_view` intersection,
per-portal interleaving of punch and interior draw.

**All three lanes state their gate's ALLOCATION cost on the default path, and all three are zero.**
A's is locked by a test that fails if the stencil expression ever mentions `portalPunch` again —
that is the 08-13 blackout wired shut.

## 2. OPEN

* **O-P2 relief — measured, and it is not free.** Valid pair (both arms armed-asserted, sky-pinned,
  real 1070): ON 14.4 fps / p50 41.7 / p90 133.4 / 929 calls / 38,985 tris per frame; OFF 15.8 /
  33.4 / 75.0 / 898 / 32,899. **+6,086 tris and +31 calls per frame, p90 nearly doubled.** The
  geometry delta is real and consistent with the mechanism. The fps figures are single 20 s samples
  dominated by streaming stalls — treat the TRIANGLE and CALL deltas as the evidence, not the fps.
  Still an owner call, and still wants a look, not just numbers.
* **O-P3 cloud ultra — INCONCLUSIVE, do not read the fps.** ultra 22.6 fps vs preset 12.1, which is
  backwards and implausible; p50 is 16.7 vs 16.8, i.e. identical steady state. The two arms had
  different streaming/warm states. Needs a re-run with a settle gate before it means anything.
* **O-P1 daylight before/after — STILL NOT SHOT.** A's and D's pairs are queued and VOID: their
  URLs point at their lanes' own serve ports (8771/8773), which are gone, and only 8765 is
  reverse-tunnelled to the 1070. Re-point both pairs to `127.0.0.1:8765` (which serves the shared
  tree, now carrying the merged code) and drain. This is the first thing to do next session.
* **O-P4 → CLOSED** by lane B. O-P5 DEC-17 got a single arm (7.6 fps, heavy p99 3 s stalls —

## 3. TRAPS PAID FOR TODAY

* **The buildbox is effectively unusable on SPOT.** `us-central1-b` (NOT `-a` — `fleet-runbooks.md`
  is stale). It preempted within ~1 minute of STAGING, twice, and never gave a shell. Eyes moved
  to the 1070 on owner instruction. Do not plan a session around it without switching to on-demand.
* **A shared pair-level assertion voids matched A/B pairs.** In a real A/B the two arms are
  DELIBERATELY in different states, so one expression cannot be true on both — the relief pair
  voided twice on its own correct OFF arm. Assertions are now PER ARM (`arm.assert`).
* **The sky-pin gate was itself lying.** `bootpin.mjs` scrapes the console for `[skytime] pinned`
  and read false on a page that was pinned. `setSkyTimeOverride` RETURNS a boolean — gate on the
  return value, and put `?skytime=13` in the URL (a boot-time numeric pin) as well.
* **ACE holds a login well past the ~25 s folklore gap.** A 45 s cooldown still gave
  `connect failed after 1 attempts: timeout` on arm 2 — the same signature 08-13 wrongly wrote off
  as a missing account. Give each ARM its own account from the agentp07–agentp10 pool.
  (`tailnet1` is the OWNER'S and is excluded by construction in the runner.)
* **`pkill -f <pattern>` where the pattern matches your own command line self-kills (exit 144).**
  Match with `ps -eo pid,args | grep -F` and kill by PID.
* Worktree provisioning that symlinks ALL of `external/chorizite`'s children also symlinks the
  TRACKED `VENDORED.md`, so every lane shows a spurious type-change on that path. Never let it ride
  along in a commit (none did).

## 4. THE RIG (reusable — this is the part worth keeping)

* `/mnt/wbterminal2/lanes/<lane>/` — per-lane worktrees. Create with the recipe in
  `scripts/parity-ab.sh` (externals symlinked, chorizite children individually, `node_modules`
  borrowed, own real release `pkg/`). **Release wasm is ~6.68 MB, not 4.5 MB.**
* `/mnt/wbterminal2/eyeq/` — the GPU evidence queue.
  * `queue.jsonl` — one PAIR per line; a pair is ATOMIC (half a pair is `void`, never interpreted).
  * `runner.mjs` — one pair per invocation: fresh chrome `--user-data-dir` per arm (shader cache),
    per-arm account, boot retry, sky-pin gate on the return value, `renderer.info.autoReset=false`
    with cumulative counters ÷ frames, canvas screenshot, `__diag` capture.
  * `drain.sh` — drains the queue pair by pair.
  * `out/<pair>/<arm>/{result.json,frame.png}` — five frames captured today.
* Lane briefs that produced this: `/mnt/wbterminal2/lanes/briefs/{PRE,A,B,D}.md`. The hard don'ts
  (no push, no self-armed automation, no `tailnet1`, no touching the shared tree) are in `PRE.md`.
